newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's not involved in T&N reinsurance deal.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's not involved in T&N reinsurance deal.

text.p: Lloyds of London underwriting syndicates are not participating in the 500 million stg reinsurance of T&N's asbestos liability, a spokesman for the insurance market told Reuters on Wednesday.

Lloyd's syndicates cannot accept 1992 or prior liabilities following the transfer of all such risks to the Equitas reinsurance company set up by Lloyd's this year as part of its reconstruction and renewal programme.

"It's not allowed under the market's bye-laws," he added. This is the first major reinsurance deal from which Lloyd's has been effectively excluded by the changes brought about by reconstruction and renewal (R&R).
Automotive components group T&N earlier announced details of a plan to limit its potential liabilities from future asbestos related claims.

The liabilities arise from the group's involvement in the mining and manufacture of asbestos earlier this century. Asbestos was widely used in car parts and the construction industry. Exposure can lead to a fatal disease known as asbestosis.
A Lloyd's underwriter told Reuters it was highly unlikely that any syndicates were involved in the T&N reinsurance package because of the restrictions placed on them by R&R.
Lloyd's insurers would also tend to avoid asbestos related risks because asbestosis was behind a large part of the market's record losses in recent years, he added.

Three international reinsurers, Munich Re, Centre Re, a part of Zurich, and Swiss Re unit European International Reinsurance, are involved in the complex deal. For a one-off 92 million stg premium they are providing T&N with up to 500 million stg cover. However, this will only be called on if claims exceed certain agreed amounts which T&N will have to pay itself.
T&N will this year put aside 323 million stg on top of the 99 million it has already set aside to cover potential claims. This figure will rise to 550 million stg over time.

The group will also be responsible for the first 58 million stg of claims above 323 million at current prices. This element of the package, which T&N calls "disclose", will rise to a maximum of 140 million stg over time.
T&N's maximum outstanding exposure is therefore 690 million stg, with reinsurers providing up to 500 million stg on top of this.
These figures are based on actuaries' pessimistic estimates, the company said.
"The insurance is worldwide and without time limit. We're talking about (needing it until) 2020 or something," T&N chairman Sir Colin Hope said.
